engine_step_at_issue: The engine allowed the Colorado sales tax refund ($19, computed from MAGI of $4,625.40) for tax year 2026. It applied the tax year 2025 refund table without the statutory condition that FY 2025-26 revenue exceed the TABOR/Referendum C cap. That condition was not met: it was projected unmet before the freeze and certified unmet in September 2026.
summary: For tax year 2026, Colorado law (C.R.S. 39-22-2003) allows the state sales tax refund only if there were excess state revenues for the fiscal year ending in that tax year, which is FY 2025-26. Every official projection before the freeze, including the June 2026 Legislative Council Staff forecast, had FY 2025-26 revenue $424.9M below the Referendum C cap, with no refund obligation, so that refund is $0. The head is 66 and childless, so no federal EITC means no CO EITC, and there is no CO CTC, FATC, senior housing credit or other refundable credit. The engine's $19 is all sales tax refund. It is the published tax year 2025 lowest-tier single-filer amount carried into 2026, an amount 2026 law does not support. The law gives $0, which matches the consensus.
